title: The Inherits field in the Create Script menu cannot be blank
body: ### Tested versions - v4.6.2.stable.steam [71f334935] ### System information Godot v4.6.2.stable (71f334935) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7628) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-3470 CPU @ 3.20GHz (4 threads) - 31.96 GiB memory ### Issue description Scripts don't require inheritance. If you're writing a utility class or a class that doesn't depend on GD Object capabilities, you can remove the "extends" line from the new file. (I've read somewhere that the engine assumes "extends Reference" by default). Such classes work in projects without a problem. When you use the "Create Script" menu, you can't leave the "Inherits" field blank, it will error with the "Invalid inherited parent name or path." message and block the "Create" button. Expectation: It'd allow to create a .gd file with a specified name, which will be a blank file or use a template, just without the "extends" line. Behavior: I can't proceed. I have to pick any class only to remove it after creating a file. This check tests if the name of the extended class is correct, but this block appears to not account for the field being empty. Since classes can just not inherit anything, this error seems to not match the engine's logic. The field could simply either account for being empty or use a checkbox like other fields. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Right-click in the FileSystem pane, select "Create New" > "Script..." 2. Leave the "Inherits" field empty. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
